A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ProDAG research. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison despite retitling, reformatting, and renumbering.

before.justification: v4 reports original synthetic-data experiments, flow-cytometry results in Table 1, computational timings, and appendix robustness experiments.

after.justification: v5 retains original synthetic and real-data evaluations and reports additional robustness results and projection timings.

M1.justification: The two-stage acyclicity/ℓ1 projection, joint-space ELBO, implicit gradients, and nonlinear extension are retained. v5's training pseudocode formalizes the existing procedure; its corrected ℓ1 pseudocode uses the acyclic input already specified in v4's prose.

E1.justification: v5 adds 20-node, 60-edge graphs, exponential-noise data, and scale-free graphs with degree exponent 3. Existing linear/nonlinear benchmarks, Sachs data, and robustness scenarios remain; the retained scale-free results are now labelled degree exponent 2.

E2.justification: BOSS is added to the real-data comparison in v5 Table 1, where it was absent in v4. Comparator membership in the corresponding synthetic experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendices D/E revise reported DiBS settings from 10 real-data particles to 50 throughout and replace consensus-based real-data sparsity selection with the general 10% validation rule; BayesDAG retains truth-based sparsity tuning. v5 also separately times batches of 100 projections. These disclosures do not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v5 extends the existing density, noise-distribution, and scale-free robustness analyses with one additional configuration each. Figure 2 also separately measures projection cost alongside the retained training-time analysis.

E5.justification: v4 Table 1 gives scores without uncertainty estimates or replication information; v5 reports averages and standard errors over 10 data splits. Synthetic experiments already report averages and standard errors over 10 datasets in both versions. An increase in run counts is not established.

E6.justification: The real-data results are substantially revised: ProDAG's Brier/SHD/F1/AUROC values change from 19.3/20.9/33%/66% to 16/18/24%/60%, with Brier performance changing from trailing DiBS to a reported tie. These are results under revised reported settings, not controlled performance changes. v5 also adds BOSS results, three robustness configurations, and projection timings; the six retained synthetic result plots are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix A revises the uniqueness argument, treats lambda = 0 separately, and adds an affine-hyperplane argument, lexicographic tie-breaking, and an invocation of Berge's maximum theorem for measurability. v5 also explicitly specifies Gaussian noise and fixed lambda in the posterior-learning exposition. The principal theorem, gradient formulas, and nonlinear reduction are retained.

C1.justification: The core claims remain valid projected DAG distributions, scalable variational inference for linear and nonlinear DAGs, and competitive accuracy and uncertainty quantification. The revised abstract and new contribution list primarily restate claims already present in v4.

C2.justification: New Appendices H and I explicitly discuss potentially poor variational approximations, stationary-point solutions arising from nonconvex optimization, and the assumptions needed to interpret observationally learned DAGs causally, including causal sufficiency and subject-matter assessment.

D1.justification: v5 adds baseline software versions and licenses, explicit training pseudocode, and the retained scale-free experiment's degree exponent. It drops v4's Gumbel(0,1) parameters and explicit nonlinear real-data specification. The toolkit statement changes from '[redacted]' to generic GitHub availability, but neither PDF supplies a specific ProDAG repository address.

R1.justification: The bibliography drops Bezanson et al. (2017), the Julia reference. The remaining cited works and the positioning relative to Bayesian DAG methods, continuous acyclicity approaches, and projection-based priors are substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v5 edits the title, abstract, and conclusion; adds a contribution list; condenses the sparsity subsection into a footnote; merges nonlinear subsections; and moves projection pseudocode into Appendix B. The main section sequence and much of the exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, with extensive resizing and redistribution of displays. v5 adds a projection schematic, a training-algorithm display, a projection-time panel, and three robustness figures. Table 1 accommodates BOSS and uncertainty reporting, while plot labels explicitly identify expected SHD and F1.

improvement.justification: v5 improves transparency through real-data uncertainty estimates, broader robustness checks, baseline version information, and explicit limitations. The schematic and training pseudocode also clarify the method. These gains outweigh limited documentation regressions, including the omitted nonlinear real-data specification and Appendix G's density multipliers, which conflict with Figures 6–7. The core method and main synthetic findings remain unchanged.
